column3: The Hebrew has a singular man and a singular fighting oppressor; BSB has plural men pressing an attack.
The Hebrew names flesh; BSB says man.
The Hebrew says plans for evil; BSB specifies his demise.
The Hebrew names his heels; BSB says steps.
The Hebrew has a singular wandering and tear and names a skin bottle; BSB has plural wanderings and tears and a bottle.
The Hebrew says this I know; BSB says by this I will know.
The Hebrew says a word without an explicit possessive; BSB supplies whose word.
The Hebrew introduces the feet with a rhetorical question; BSB gives a coordinated statement.
